placeholder_patterns: hard cut into the dialogue beat with the speaker mid-line
hard cut to the reaction as the line lands
the subject is already moving inside the storyboard framing
the room falls quiet around it
reacts as the line lands, no static hold

1_single_driving_question_per_block.description: Cada bloque de 6 escenas (1 minuto) tiene UNA sola pregunta dramática que lo impulsa; ninguna escena del bloque puede abrir una pregunta nueva.

2_strict_cause_and_effect_chain.description: De la escena 2 a la 60, cada escena declara la consecuencia de la anterior, la acción concreta con la que arranca y el único cambio de estado con el que termina.

3_no_location_ping_pong.description: Agrupa de 3 a 5 escenas consecutivas en la misma locación. Prohibido volver a una locación tras una sola escena en otra (patrón A-B-A).

4_canonical_object_lock.description: Cada escena usa un único nombre exacto de key_object en el panel de storyboard, en la acción de la Toma 1 y en la lista Key Object. No se admiten alias ni variantes.

5_disorder_test_validation.description: Si se desordena el bloque y la cadena causal deja de tener sentido, el validador lo rechaza. También rechaza placeholders de cámara y ping-pong de locaciones.

acts.title: The Bait
acts.goal: Open a visceral question in the first 3 seconds, establish the protagonist's desire and wound, then detonate the inciting incident.
must_happen: Scene 1 poses an unanswered question or a visual contradiction (no slow establishing montage).
The protagonist wants something concrete and is denied it by someone with power.
The antagonist is introduced as reasonable and likable, never cartoonish.
Scene 10 reveals a secret object, document, witness or betrayal that changes the question.
acts.retention_device: Open loop stacked on a second open loop; every scene ends on a partial answer that creates a new question.
acts.dopamine_point: Scene 8-10: first small act of defiance from the protagonist.

acts.title: The Trap
acts.goal: Tighten the trap: the antagonist uses the system, not violence. Humiliation and betrayal push the protagonist toward a forced choice.
must_happen: The protagonist's credibility or livelihood is threatened in public.
A trusted ally withholds information or signs something they should not.
The antagonist offers a deal the protagonist cannot easily refuse.
Scene 20 ends on a demand, a deadline or a public accusation.
acts.retention_device: Countdown pressure (hearing, deadline, debt) plus dramatic irony: the audience learns the truth before the town does.
acts.dopamine_point: Scene 17-18: a first piece of evidence lands in the protagonist's hands.

acts.title: The First Crack
acts.goal: The protagonist stops reacting and starts investigating. A romance or loyalty beat raises the emotional stakes. A costly mistake keeps the antagonist ahead.
must_happen: The protagonist takes a concrete risk (break-in, trespass, public question, leaked file).
The audience gets a hard piece of proof the town does not yet believe.
A romance or intimacy beat complicates the alliance.
The antagonist counterattacks using the protagonist's own action against her/him.
Scene 30 ends on a temptation or a compromise that could destroy the case.
acts.retention_device: Proof vs. believability: the protagonist has the truth but not the power to make anyone believe it.
acts.dopamine_point: Scene 24-25: discovery of the physical evidence (ledger, recording, permit, logbook).

acts.title: The Dark Night
acts.goal: Take everything away. The ally breaks, the institution turns, and the protagonist is isolated. The lowest point must be caused by a choice, not bad luck.
must_happen: The protagonist rejects the antagonist's deal and pays an immediate price.
The institution (court, trust, employer, town council) freezes or seizes something vital.
The ally's betrayal is explained by a credible threat, not villainy.
The protagonist loses the physical evidence or access to it.
Scene 40 ends with a new interpretation of an old object/place (the lighthouse, the house, the boathouse).
acts.retention_device: All-is-lost engine: the audience wants to see how the protagonist climbs out, not whether she deserves to.
acts.dopamine_point: Scene 35-36: a micro-revenge line or a quiet power move that costs the protagonist something.

acts.title: The Turn
acts.goal: The protagonist turns the same system against the antagonist using the truth she already had. The confrontation begins in public. A final complication raises the price of winning.
must_happen: The protagonist converts a discarded detail into leverage (logbook, timestamp, witness, receipt).
The antagonist's power is shown to depend on the town's belief, which can be broken.
A public or semi-public confrontation forces the antagonist to drop the mask.
The ally earns a partial redemption through a costly action.
Scene 50 ends on the antagonist's last threat or a new piece of evidence that reframes the case.
acts.retention_device: Power flip: the audience now knows the protagonist can win, but not at what cost.
acts.dopamine_point: Scene 47-49: the protagonist says the line the audience has been waiting ten episodes for.

acts.title: The Payoff
acts.goal: Deliver the public confrontation, the emotional payoff and the romantic resolution. End on a new open loop for the next episode.
must_happen: The truth is exposed in a public, irreversible way (hearing, broadcast, town meeting).
The antagonist loses the specific thing they used to control the protagonist.
The protagonist chooses what she keeps, not only what she destroys.
A romantic or familial payoff lands in one concrete gesture, not a speech.
Scene 59 or 60 plants the next-episode hook in a single line or object.
acts.retention_device: Payoff + new question: close the season question and open a second, more personal mystery in the last 20 seconds.
acts.dopamine_point: Scene 56-59: public humiliation of the antagonist and the protagonist's final refusal.

viral_latam_to_usa_templates.name: The Ranch Laundress and the Stolen Heirloom
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.premise: A humble ranch laundress is publicly accused of stealing the family heirloom. The real thief is a wealthy family member, and the heir she loves is the only one willing to prove her innocence.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.protagonist: A proud ranch laundress humiliated in front of the whole family.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.antagonist: The entitled relative who planted the heirloom and the matriarch who protects the family name.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.love_interest: The heir who risks his inheritance to defend her.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.hook: They accused the help. The thief wore the family name.
structure: Public humiliation: the heirloom disappears during a family gathering and the laundress is accused.
A physical detail contradicts the accusation: mud on the wrong boots, a broken clasp, a locked room.
The heir investigates and discovers the planted evidence and the family cover-up.
The laundress is forced to leave; the heir stops her at the gate with proof.
Public reveal before the family and the town: the real thief is exposed.
Payoff: the laundress is vindicated, the heir chooses her, and a new family secret opens.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.usa_adaptation: Texas or Montana ranch, county fair or ranch anniversary party, US English, land and class stakes, conservative family dynasty.

viral_latam_to_usa_templates.name: The Humiliated Vagabond Is the Billionaire Owner
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.premise: A humble ranch hand arrives at the property and is humiliated by the corrupt foreman and the family, never suspecting that he is the new billionaire owner who bought the entire ranch.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.protagonist: A quiet, underestimated ranch hand disguised as a drifter.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.antagonist: The corrupt foreman and the family that treats the newcomer like trash.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.love_interest: The ranch worker who treats him with dignity when nobody else does.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.hook: They threw out the man who owns the land.
structure: Humiliation: the drifter is mocked, underpaid and thrown out of the ranch house.
The heroine defends him and loses her job for it.
The drifter returns as the anonymous billionaire owner and quietly changes the power dynamic.
The corrupt foreman tries to cover up the abuse and frames the heroine.
Public reveal: the owner identifies himself and exposes the foreman's fraud.
Payoff: the heroine is chosen, the foreman faces the consequences, and a new threat appears.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.usa_adaptation: Texas or Montana cattle ranch, US English, ranch-hand class conflict, land ownership and public status reversal.

viral_latam_to_usa_templates.name: The Hidden Will and the Secret Daughter
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.premise: A young woman enters the ranch as a maid to find the true will hidden under the floorboards or in a secret drawer by the ambitious widow and the family lawyer.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.protagonist: The young maid who is secretly the rightful daughter and heir.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.antagonist: The ambitious widow and the lawyer who forged the current will.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.love_interest: The heir or ranch manager who chooses the truth over the inheritance.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.hook: The will named a daughter no one had ever met.
structure: The maid arrives at the ranch and is treated as invisible by the widow and the lawyer.
A loose floorboard or locked drawer reveals a second, older will.
The widow accuses the maid of theft and forgery before the family.
The maid finds a birth record, photograph or letter proving she is the secret daughter.
Public hearing: the lawyer's forgery is exposed and the widow loses control.
Payoff: the maid claims her name and inheritance, and a new family secret opens.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.usa_adaptation: Texas or Montana ranch estate, US English, probate hearing, legitimacy and family-dynasty stakes.

viral_latam_to_usa_templates.name: Contract Marriage with the Proud Foreman
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.premise: To save her late father's ranch from bank ruin, the protagonist must marry her proud rival by contract. In secret, he protects her from an internal betrayal that wants to take the land.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.protagonist: The determined rancher's daughter hiding the family's bankruptcy.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.antagonist: The relative or bank ally who wants the ranch and exposes the contract.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.love_interest: The proud foreman who signs the contract for his own secret reason.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.hook: She bought a husband for one year. He wanted the truth.
structure: The bank deadline forces the contract marriage to be signed in public.
Forced proximity reveals the foreman's secret debt and the heroine's collapsing ranch.
Sabotage at the ranch puts the heroine in danger and the foreman protects her.
The antagonist exposes the contract to humiliate them; the couple turns it into a real commitment.
Public confrontation: the sabotage is traced to the antagonist.
Payoff: the contract is torn up, a real proposal lands, and a new threat appears.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.usa_adaptation: Texas or Wyoming ranch, US English, bank foreclosure, blue-collar vs. landowner class tension.

viral_latam_to_usa_templates.name: The Untamable Champion Horse
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.setting: Kentucky horse farm or Texas ranch
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.premise: A champion horse that nobody on the ranch can ride is tamed by the humblest worker on the property. The feat saves the ranch from ruin and awakens a forbidden love.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.protagonist: The humble ranch worker with a natural gift for horses.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.antagonist: The rival stable owner and the ranch manager who wants the horse destroyed.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.love_interest: The owner's heir who is promised to another family.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.hook: The horse that broke every rider chose the one nobody saw.
structure: The untamable champion injures another rider and the ranch is threatened with foreclosure.
The humblest worker is blamed and forbidden from entering the stable.
A hidden injury or doped feed reveals the rival stable's sabotage.
The worker bonds with the horse and proves the method works before the championship.
Public race: the sabotage is exposed and the rival stable is disqualified.
Payoff: the horse wins, the forbidden love is chosen, and a new race or threat opens.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.usa_adaptation: Kentucky or Texas horse country, US English, championship race, forbidden romance and animal stakes.

viral_latam_to_usa_templates.name: Grandma's Buried Secret and the Family Betrayal
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.setting: Texas ranch or Louisiana family estate
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.premise: A grandmother despised by her ambitious children reveals a secret buried for decades and gives the inheritance to the only person who cared for her with nobility.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.protagonist: The granddaughter or caregiver who treats the matriarch with dignity.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.antagonist: The ambitious children who built their lives on the stolen family fortune.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.love_interest: The childhood friend or outsider who helps her uncover the truth.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.hook: Grandma left a box in the ground and a warning on the lid.
structure: At the family gathering, the despised grandmother announces a buried secret.
The ambitious children deny it and threaten the protagonist's inheritance.
A buried box, land deed or photograph proves the fortune was stolen from another branch.
The family destroys evidence and tries to run the protagonist out of town.
Public reveal at the family business or town meeting: the betrayal is exposed.
Payoff: the inheritance goes to the noble caregiver, and a second grave or name opens the next mystery.
viral_latam_to_usa_templates.usa_adaptation: Texas ranch or Louisiana family estate, US English, funeral and land-deed stakes, matriarch inheritance and family-business betrayal.

open_loop_types: unanswered question in the first line
person who knows more than they admit
deadline announced by a third party
public accusation with no proof yet
a lie the audience can see
retention_engine.dopamine_cadence: Every 2-3 scenes deliver one of: reveal, comeback line, protective gesture, status flip, romantic near-miss, micro-revenge, public embarrassment of the antagonist.
cliffhanger_types: new evidence that reframes the case
protagonist uses the antagonist's own weapon
a door opens on a person who should be dead or absent
forbidden: villain monologue explaining the whole plan
resolution by accident, weather or coincidence
characters withholding information for no reason
melodrama without a concrete physical stake
cliffhanger that negates the previous episode's payoff

scene_contract.dialogue: 6-15 spoken words total per scene, hard max 15. Native US English, subtext over exposition. Dialogue must finish before 8.5 seconds. Optional second line from another character.
scene_contract.internal_cuts: Exactly 3 shots inside the 10 seconds. Shot 1 runs 00s-03s and starts in motion from the storyboard panel framing. Hard cut at 3.0s to a close-up or over-the-shoulder dialogue/action shot. Hard cut at 7.0s to a tight close-up, reaction or insert. No static first frame and no extra cuts.
scene_contract.first_frame: The storyboard panel is the literal first frame of shot 1: same framing, same camera position, same wardrobe, same location, same light and same blocking. Shot 1 begins in motion from that frame. Center-weight the subject so a 9:16 crop still works.
scene_contract.audio: Native audio only: dialogue, breath, cloth, footsteps, wind, rain, room tone, diegetic SFX. No music in the generated clip (the soundtrack is mixed in post).
scene_contract.no_text: No subtitles, captions, logos, watermarks, UI or readable text rendered inside the image or video.
scene_contract.continuity: Track wardrobe, hair, injuries, props and time of day per act. A scene may not teleport to a new location without a line or a visual transition. Continuity notes describe only the present state of the scene; never reference future scenes.

continuity_rules.wardrobe: Lock one outfit per character per act; change it only at an act break with a story reason.
continuity_rules.props: The evidence object must be visible or referenced in at least 4 scenes across different acts.
continuity_rules.time_of_day: Acts 1-2 late afternoon to night; act 3 night; act 4 storm night; acts 5-6 next morning to dusk.
continuity_rules.locations: Reuse 3-5 primary locations maximum so the audience learns the geography. Group 3-6 consecutive scenes in the same dramatic situation before changing location, and bridge every location change with a line, a visual transition or a travel beat.
continuity_rules.identity: Reference images define faces. Every character in a scene must carry a cast-sheet position and a visible identity anchor: name, position number, stable descriptor and wardrobe. Never describe age, eye color or base hair color in prompts; describe only transient state (hair style, wet hair, flush, sweat, expression, wardrobe).

dialogue_rules.language: Native US English only. No translated-sounding lines.
dialogue_rules.style: Short sentences. Concrete nouns. One subtext line per scene. No therapy-speak, no lecture, no exposition dumps.
dialogue_rules.tone: Restrained, adult, cinematic. Fear and desire are shown through what characters refuse to say.

story_system.causal_order: Scenes must advance in strict cause-and-effect order. A consequence may never appear before its cause, and no clue may be revealed twice. Every act ends on a decision that forces the next act.
story_system.location_blocks: Plan 3-6 consecutive scenes inside one continuous dramatic situation before changing location. A location change needs a visible or spoken transition; no teleporting.
story_system.storyboard_sync: Each scene has exactly one storyboard panel. That panel is the literal first frame of shot 1: same framing, camera position, blocking, wardrobe, light and key object. Shot 1 begins in motion from that exact image.
story_system.identity_anchor: Every scene prompt lists each present character as: Name (Cast Sheet Pos #N: stable descriptor wearing act wardrobe). The cast sheet uses fixed left-to-right positions and uppercase names.
story_system.shot_plan: Shot 1 00s-03s: storyboard framing, subject already moving. Shot 2 03s-07s: hard cut to close-up or over-the-shoulder dialogue/action. Shot 3 07s-10s: hard cut to tight close-up, reaction or insert for the turn.
story_system.dialogue_budget: Maximum 15 spoken words per scene and dialogue must end before 8.5 seconds. Short lines, concrete nouns, no exposition dumps.
forbidden: clue revealed in an earlier act and discovered again later
inserting the reference sheet between scenes

items.label: The Secret Billionaire Divorce
items.description: Esposa o esposo humilde es despreciado y divorciado sin que sepan que es el magnate dueño del grupo empresarial.
items.protagonist: Maya Reed, the overlooked spouse who secretly controls Hartwell Global
items.antagonist: Diana Hartwell, the family matriarch who built her social power on erasing Maya
items.ally: Noah Price, the family lawyer who kept Maya's original trust documents
items.premise_seed: For six years, Maya Reed has been the invisible spouse of the Hartwell family: mocked at dinners, erased from the company directory, and finally handed divorce papers by her husband, Grant. No one knows that the 'temp' they humiliate owns the controlling shares of Hartwell Global, the group Grant's mother is desperate to save. When the board meets to strip her of everything, Maya walks in with the original trust documents and the one signature that can end their empire before lunch.
items.opening_hook: Grant slides the divorce papers across a boardroom table while his mother tells Maya she was never family; Maya calmly signs — then asks the board to read the ownership clause.
must_include: public humiliation by the spouse's family
secret ownership proof revealed at a board meeting
one ally who preserved the documents
a public reversal where the powerful family must ask for mercy
items.visual_signature: cold blue glass and marble against Maya's warm neutral tailoring; expensive suits, restrained jewelry, power expressed through silence and documents
items.series_hook: Maya does not want the company back. She wants the name of the person who erased her mother from the shareholder registry.

items.label: The Heartland Ranch Heiress
items.description: Trabajadora o peón humillado en un rancho resulta ser el heredero legítimo o comprador multimillonario.
items.protagonist: Jessie Mae Carter, a stable hand who has worked the Double Spur for nine years
items.antagonist: Harlan Caldwell Jr., the eldest son who fires her and accuses her of stealing
items.ally: Ada Bell, the county lawyer who arrives with the sealed will
items.premise_seed: At the Double Spur Ranch in Montana, Jessie Mae Carter works dawn to dark for the Caldwell family, sleeping above the tack room and eating with the hands. The morning after old man Caldwell dies, his eldest son fires her, accuses her of stealing the herd, and has her truck searched in front of the bunkhouse. The will that arrives with the county lawyer names Jessie as the sole heir of the twelve-thousand-acre spread — and the silent buyer who has been circling the ranch is her own land trust.
items.opening_hook: Jessie is ordered out of the bunkhouse in the rain while the Caldwell sons toast their inheritance; the county lawyer's car turns up the drive with a sealed envelope.
must_include: public humiliation of a ranch worker
sealed will naming the worker as sole heir
a land trust or billionaire buyer reveal
the family forced to ask the heir for mercy
items.visual_signature: wide Big Sky landscapes, dust and frost, worn denim and leather against the Caldwells' polished boots and new trucks
items.series_hook: The deed carries a second name Jessie has never seen: her mother's maiden name, dated the week she disappeared.

items.label: First Class Karma
items.description: Gerente o persona clasista humilla en Primera Clase, concesionario de lujo u hospital a alguien vestido sencillo que resulta ser el dueño o cirujano eminencia.
items.protagonist: Dr. Ava Sinclair, chief of surgery and the hidden owner of the dealership group
items.antagonist: Trevor Hale, the showroom manager who judges her by her work clothes
items.ally: Nora Kim, the general manager who answers to the board
items.premise_seed: At a Dallas luxury dealership, manager Trevor Hale refuses to let a woman in worn scrubs and no makeup sit inside the showroom car. He mocks her in front of the staff, calls security, and tells her the service entrance is around back. The woman is Dr. Ava Sinclair, chief of surgery at St. Jude's and the sole owner of the dealership's parent group. She leaves without a word. Ninety minutes later she returns with the purchase agreement, the board, and the one customer Trevor cannot afford to lose.
items.opening_hook: A security guard puts a hand on Ava's arm while Trevor laughs with a customer; Ava looks at the camera, then at the dealership name on the glass.
must_include: classist humiliation in a public luxury space
quiet identity reveal
institutional reversal with board or hospital authority
the humiliated person refuses revenge that would hurt innocent staff
items.visual_signature: polished chrome and glass against hospital whites; Ava's plain scrubs become the most powerful uniform in the room
items.series_hook: Ava buys the dealership for one reason: the previous owner was the surgeon who covered up her sister's death.

items.label: The Silver-Hair Inheritance
items.description: Madre o abuela despreciada por hijos ambiciosos revela su fortuna oculta y la entrega en el testamento a quien la cuidó con nobleza.
items.protagonist: Anna Whitaker, the granddaughter who stayed
items.co_protagonist: Rose Whitaker, the grandmother everyone underestimated
items.antagonist: Claire Whitaker, the eldest daughter who wants the lake house sold
items.premise_seed: For twenty years, Rose Whitaker has been treated like a burden by her three successful children, shuffled between guest rooms and forgotten on holidays. Only her granddaughter, Anna, stayed: cooking, driving her to appointments, and never asking for a cent. When the family gathers to move Rose into a care home and sell her lake house, the estate lawyer arrives with a sealed trust. Rose owns half the town's waterfront, and her will leaves every share to the one person who treated her like family.
items.opening_hook: Rose's daughter tells her to sign the care-home papers while Anna is in the kitchen washing dishes; Rose quietly asks the lawyer to wait in the car.
must_include: family gathering that treats the elder as a burden
hidden fortune revealed by an estate lawyer
will read that rewards the caregiver
greedy relatives forced to face their own behavior
items.visual_signature: warm wood, lake light, and silver hair; the family's expensive watches and cold manners contrast with Anna's flourishes of care
items.series_hook: The trust has a condition: Anna must live in the lake house for one year, or the fortune returns to the family that abandoned Rose.

items.label: The Gala Reckoning
items.description: Traicionada por su prometido y hermanastra tras sacrificarse por él, regresa en una gala de alta sociedad con su verdadera identidad poderosa.
items.protagonist: Clara Bennett, the fiancée who funded Julian's rise
items.antagonist: Julian Cross, the ambitious lawyer, and Vivian Bennett, the stepsister
items.ally: Mara Quinn, a society reporter who kept the receipts
items.premise_seed: Clara Bennett sold her apartment, her car, and her name to put her fiancé, Julian Cross, through law school and launch his political career. The night before the governor's gala, she finds him in the arms of her stepsister, Vivian, and is thrown out of the family home as a gold digger. Three years later, Clara returns to the same gala as the managing partner of the firm auditing Julian's campaign — and as the daughter of the man whose name the city never stopped honoring.
items.opening_hook: Clara stands in the rain outside the gala she paid for, holding a torn invitation; inside, Julian toasts Vivian as the woman who 'saved' him.
must_include: sacrifice documented in receipts, loans, or a ledger
public betrayal by fiancé and stepsister
gala return with a powerful true identity
restrained revenge that exposes the truth without violence
items.visual_signature: black-tie glamour, crystal chandeliers, rain on glass; Clara's return look is precise, expensive, and almost unrecognizable
items.series_hook: The audit file contains one line Clara cannot explain: a payment signed by her own mother, dated after her funeral.

items.label: The Quiet Hero
items.description: Veterano militar regresa a casa de incógnito, descubre abusos contra su familia y restaura el honor con su verdadero rango y recursos.
items.protagonist: Staff Sergeant Marcus Hale, home after eight years and three deployments
items.antagonist: Mayor Dale Kessler and his son, Brandt
items.ally: Lena Hale, his sister, who kept the family diner open
items.premise_seed: Staff Sergeant Marcus Hale comes home to a small Ohio town after eight years and three deployments, wearing a cheap jacket and saying nothing about the medal in his bag. He finds his sister's diner on the edge of foreclosure, his mother's medical bills sold to a collection agency, and the mayor's son bragging about the charity that is dragging his family under. When the mayor tries to use the veterans' parade as a campaign photo op, Marcus steps to the microphone with his real rank, his service record, and a federal grant the town cannot refuse.
items.opening_hook: Marcus steps off a Greyhound bus in the rain and sees his sister's diner window boarded up; a parade banner with the mayor's face hangs across the street.
must_include: undercover homecoming
abuse against the veteran's family
public restoration of honor
resources used to protect the town, not just to punish
items.visual_signature: flat Ohio winter light, worn work jacket and duffel bag, American flags and campaign bunting, quiet dignity instead of spectacle
items.series_hook: The federal grant was written for a soldier who died on Marcus's last mission. Marcus has to decide whether to use it in that soldier's name.

teaser_rules.teaser_1: Scenes 1-6: the hook, the world and the first open loop. Must work with zero context.
teaser_rules.teaser_2: The mid-story twist or the strongest romantic beat. Use 6 consecutive scenes from acts 3-4.
teaser_rules.teaser_3: The cliffhanger or the confrontation. Use 6 consecutive scenes from acts 5-6.
teaser_rules.hook_text: 5-10 words, all caps allowed for one word, no spoilers, ends with an open loop.
teaser_rules.caption: 2-4 short lines, one question, 4-8 niche hashtags, honest CTA (follow/save/comment), no fake DM promises.
